subject: Pharmacology
summary: Low Molecular Weight Heparin (LMWH) is a subcutaneous anticoagulant that mainly inhibits factor Xa, providing predictable anticoagulation without routine lab monitoring. It is used for VTE prophylaxis and treatment, especially in hospitalised and high‑risk patients.

sections.p: LMWHs are derived from unfractionated heparin and have a shorter chain length, giving them a higher anti‑Xa to anti‑IIa activity ratio. They are given by subcutaneous injection and have a longer half‑life, allowing once‑ or twice‑daily dosing.
b: Predictable pharmacokinetics → no routine coagulation monitoring
Lower risk of heparin‑induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) than UFH
Renally cleared – dose adjust in renal impairment

sections.p: LMWH binds antithrombin III, accelerating its inhibition of factor Xa (and to a lesser extent thrombin). This blocks conversion of prothrombin to thrombin, preventing fibrin clot formation.

t.b: Is therapeutic anticoagulation achieved? 0.5‑1.0 IU/mL (therapeutic) or 0.2‑0.5 IU/mL (prophylactic). Low result → under‑anticoagulated; high → bleeding risk.
Detects HIT. Drop >50 % or <150 ×10⁹/L after 5‑10 days suggests HIT; stop LMWH.
Guides dose adjustment. eGFR <30 mL/min → reduce dose or avoid LMWH.

sections.p: LMWH dosing follows weight‑based protocols and is adjusted for renal function, pregnancy, and bleeding risk. No routine INR monitoring is needed, unlike warfarin.
b: Avoid in severe hepatic disease with coagulopathy

sections.p: Bleeding is the main adverse effect; HIT is rare but serious. Accumulation in renal failure can cause supratherapeutic anti‑Xa levels and major hemorrhage.
b: Major bleed → stop LMWH, give protamine (partial reversal)
HIT → discontinue LMWH, switch to a non‑heparin anticoagulant
Renal impairment → monitor anti‑Xa, adjust dose

sections.p: LMWH is first‑line for VTE prophylaxis in medical and surgical patients, treatment of acute DVT/PE, and bridging to oral anticoagulants. It is safe in pregnancy and cancer‑associated thrombosis.

t.b: Confirms DVT presence; positive → start therapeutic LMWH.

sections.p: Key points to remember for exams: LMWH’s anti‑Xa focus, reduced HIT risk, dosing adjustments, and reversal strategy.
b: LMWH > UFH for VTE prophylaxis in most patients
Anti‑Xa level used only in renal failure, obesity, or pregnancy

whenToSeekHelp: Sudden severe chest pain or dyspnoea (possible PE)
Unexplained drop in haemoglobin or overt bleeding
New onset thrombocytopenia with skin lesions

faq.q: Why is routine INR monitoring not required with LMWH?
faq.a: LMWH has predictable pharmacokinetics and a fixed anti‑Xa:anti‑IIa ratio, so dose‑response is stable without INR checks.

faq.q: Can LMWH be used in patients with severe kidney disease?
faq.a: Use with caution; dose‑adjust or switch to unfractionated heparin if eGFR <30 mL/min.

exam: Explain the mechanism by which LMWH prevents clot formation and why it has a lower HIT risk than UFH.
A pregnant woman with a DVT is started on anticoagulation. Which drug is preferred and why?
Describe how you would adjust LMWH dosing in a patient with an eGFR of 25 mL/min.
